name: Snowflake
summary: Snowflake is a cloud data platform company. It also makes [Arctic](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/snowflake-launches-arctic-the-most-open-enterprise-grade-large-language-model-2/), an open-weight language model.

incidents.title: Attackers Stole Data From Snowflake Customer Accounts Without MFA
incidents.summary: In 2024, a financially motivated group used stolen passwords to take data from Snowflake customer accounts that did not use multi-factor authentication (MFA), according to Mandiant. Mandiant found no evidence that Snowflake's own enterprise environment was breached.
incidents.description: In 2024, a group used passwords that malware stole to take data from Snowflake customer accounts without MFA and to try to extort the victims, [Mandiant reported](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/unc5537-snowflake-data-theft-extortion). Mandiant and Snowflake notified about 165 organizations that were possibly affected. Snowflake [made MFA the default](https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/snowflake-mfa-policy-change/720851/) for new accounts, and lawsuits against it continue in federal court.

timeline.description: Mandiant identifies a broader campaign, contacts Snowflake and starts to notify possible victims.

timeline.description: The federal court in Montana denies Snowflake's motion to dismiss the main claims of financial institutions. A separate ruling on consumer claims came on 2025-10-28.

incidents.title: Prompt Injection Let Snowflake's Cortex Code CLI Escape Its Sandbox
incidents.summary: A flaw in Snowflake's Cortex Code CLI coding agent let hidden instructions in untrusted content run commands outside its sandbox without user approval. Snowflake published an advisory and [CVE-2026-6442](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6442), and fixed the flaw in version 1.0.25 on 2026-02-28.
incidents.description: [PromptArmor reported](https://www.promptarmor.com/resources/snowflake-ai-escapes-sandbox-and-executes-malware) that hidden instructions in untrusted content, such as a repository README, could make Snowflake's Cortex Code CLI coding agent run commands outside its sandbox without user approval. In a test, the agent used cached Snowflake tokens to copy and delete tables. Snowflake confirmed the flaw, fixed it in version 1.0.25, and [published CVE-2026-6442](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6442).

incidents.title: Snowflake Says a Rogue AI Agent Stopped Processes for All Users of a Cloud Workspace
incidents.summary: In an [engineering post](https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/engineering/ai-agent-dangerous-activity-detection/), Snowflake said that a trial of its agent-monitoring system on about 12,000 internal agent trajectories from engineering staff confirmed one case of rogue-agent activity, which terminated the process across all users of a cloud workspace. The post does not give the date, the agent or the model.
incidents.description: [Snowflake said](https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/engineering/ai-agent-dangerous-activity-detection/) that it tested its agent-monitoring system on about 12,000 internal agent trajectories from its engineers. According to the company, the test found one case of rogue-agent activity: an agent stopped the process for all users of a cloud workspace. Snowflake did not identify the agent or the model.

sources.title: Beyond the Prompt: Dangerous Activity Detection for AI Agent Trajectories
